authority.gating: only a proven finding whose blocks denies the requested intent
authority.readiness_scope: the v1 code subset only, never the ten-axis model
authority.rollup_authority_note: the numeric rollup never gates; 'the scorer is the gate' was withdrawn post-reveal because a number an agent can optimize becomes the target

axes.question: Are there named, non-interactive commands with stable exit semantics?
axes.title: Entrypoint clarity

axes.question: Do the declared units cover the serial oracle, with explicit exclusions?
axes.title: Selection completeness

axes.question: Are temp/output/cache paths and repo-root assumptions per-run and portable?
axes.title: Workspace isolation

axes.question: Are databases, caches and containers namespaced, owned, health-checked and torn down?
axes.title: Service isolation

axes.question: Do shared files, singleton locks, global ports or order dependence break concurrent runs?
axes.title: Concurrency safety

axes.question: Do repeated runs agree, with fixed seeds and no unpinned time/network/image inputs?
axes.title: Determinism

axes.question: Are OS, architecture, tooling, memory/disk, secrets and network posture declared?
axes.title: Resource declaration

axes.question: Are exit codes, logs, reports and artifact paths machine-readable and bounded?
axes.title: Observability

axes.question: Does the suite behave on a dirty tree, with generated prerequisites and pinned toolchains?
axes.title: Source fidelity

axes.question: On timeout or failure, are child processes, services and workspaces actually cleaned up?
axes.title: Failure cleanup

codes.detects: the big suite has no cross-machine partition vocabulary (in-process sharding is not one)
codes.invariant: the suite can be partitioned into disjoint subsets addressable from the CLI

codes.detects: the only entrypoint serializes itself, so an external scheduler cannot own ordering
codes.invariant: the suite exposes a way to run its work without taking its own global lock

codes.detects: test packages exist that no declared entrypoint runs, so the unit union is not the suite
codes.invariant: every test-bearing package is reachable from a declared aggregate entrypoint

codes.detects: ../.. or absolute paths threaded through targets break the moment the tree moves
codes.invariant: no target depends on an absolute path or a path that escapes the repo root

codes.detects: proof exists only whole-tree, so a fanned-out run cannot be aggregated honestly
codes.invariant: proof of a run composes from per-unit evidence

codes.detects: a fixed port or fixed socket path makes two concurrent runs collide
codes.invariant: service endpoints are allocated per run and injected by environment

codes.detects: every declared lane needs a database, cache or container to start
codes.invariant: at least one declared lane runs to completion with no external service

codes.detects: a floating tag means two runs of the same tree can test different software
codes.invariant: every external service image is pinned by digest

codes.detects: service markers are maintained by hand, so the service-free lane drifts silently
codes.invariant: a test's service requirement is derived from what it requests, not hand-labelled

codes.detects: the gate is an && chain, so a phase cannot be placed or retried on its own
codes.invariant: the declared gate is separately invocable lanes, not one chain of phases
